renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: His waking comes from your waking, his sleep from your sleep. So everything's got your nature: the world is real and not real.
Here's where rituals run out: tongue's too tired for your name, mind's too tired for remembering you. Meditate on what has no shape? Name what has no qualities?
You who are full — where do we put the welcome party? You who hold everything — where's your chair? Wash-water and cheers for the clean one? A sip for the pure?
A bath for the stainless? Clothes for the guy whose belly is the world? Perfume for the no-smell one? Jewelry for the pretty one?
Holy string for the guy with no supports? Flowers for the wanter of nothing? Incense for the noseless, a lamp for the eyeless — what's the point?
Snacks for the never-hungry, a chew for the Lord — so where? Walk-arounds for the endless, bowing for the no-two-er — so where?
Lamp-wavings for the self-lit Boss? And how do you order up a hymn for the One the holy books can't even talk about?
How do you throw him a goodbye party when he's full inside and out? And how do you burn an offering for the no-difference guy, everywhere?
Where's the fee for Mr. Full? A drink for the always-content? Walking papers for the everywhere guy? Forgiveness for the never-seen?
Exactly like that is the top worship, in every state, all the time: mind with no twos in it, hitch it to God who owns everything.
